name: Keep a searchable knowledge base of the business
summary: Keeps a searchable knowledge base of the business: it gathers the SOPs, pages and docs the business already has into one indexed store, writes new entries from them as draft pages in Confluence, and publishes each entry once a person approves it. Crons read and draft; a person approves every publish.

covered_by.capture-knowledge: gather (existing Confluence pages and Google Docs become sources); walkthrough recordings are a person's step
covered_by.gather-existing: gather (sources stored once, refreshed each hour)
covered_by.write-entry: skill (outline into a proposal), then draft (entry as a draft page in Confluence)
covered_by.review-approve: approval (a person reads the draft page and approves the publish)
covered_by.publish: approval (publish to the knowledge base space)
covered_by.share-with-team: not yet (see gaps): space access is set in Confluence by a person
covered_by.search-lookup: the sources store the agent searches; staff use Confluence search
covered_by.update-stale: gather flags pages whose last version is past the limit; revising them is a person's step
covered_by.record-keeping: the sources store holds each source's status and its entry; no platform log

crons.name: gather
crons.summary: Existing pages and docs: one stored source each, refreshed, with stale pages flagged.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Write each source that has an outline into a draft Confluence page, queue its publish for approval, and mark published entries.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: a read of existing pages and docs, and a Confluence page in draft that only its editor can see. Publishing an entry to the knowledge base space is a live operation and waits for a person.

confluence.covers: existing pages read from a source space; entries created as drafts in the knowledge base space; publish on approval

google-workspace.covers: existing Google Docs read from one Drive folder; text read for search and for writing entries

gaps: Microsoft 365: the mapped operations are Outlook mail and Excel tables only, with no SharePoint, OneDrive or OneNote content. Not built.
Share-with-team (Google Drive sharing, Confluence space permissions): sharing reaches staff and so waits for a person. No sharing operation is queued by a cron.
Claude and GPT (the most named tools): the model is the agent, not a kit platform. Writing an outline is a skill step.
Loom and other walkthrough recorders: not platforms in the kit. Recordings are made and linked by the owner; no transcript is pulled.
Hubspot, Aircall AI, Notion and other tools: no mapped knowledge-base operations here.
Staleness for Google Docs: Drive returns no modified date through the mapped parameters, so Docs are never flagged as stale.
Revising an existing page (update-stale): the draft cron only creates new entries. Changes to a page that is already live are a person's step.
Google Doc drafting: entries are written to Confluence only. Drafting a Doc needs a move into the folder through drive.files.update, not built.
Confluence publish takes the draft's version number plus one. That is the rule for updating a page, but it is unverified on a sandbox space.
Platform help: none of the three platforms' supplied help pages describe knowledge base steps, so every step's support is marked unknown until a live account confirms it.
Every adapter is docs-only until a Confluence sandbox space and a Google Workspace test account prove it.
